title: fix(import): mesh rational B-spline thread strips closed and at full fidelity
body:
## What changed

The rational `B_SPLINE_SURFACE` faces of #1602's parts are thread flanks and roots. Each is one strip, degree 1 across and degree 2 along, in 36-degree arcs, about fourteen turns long. truck meshed each one into ~2 M facets with a 0.5-3 mm hole. Three causes, all fixed in the importer's wrapper around a face (`step_guard::Metered`), with truck itself unchanged:

1. **Facet runaway: the division split both directions.** truck's `parameter_division` flags BOTH intervals of a cell that fails its bilinear test. A strip curved only along v therefore gets 2^sweeps intervals across u. The new `step_division` tests each cell's iso-v chord (splits u) and iso-u chord (splits v) separately, and it falls back to truck's bilinear test (which splits both) only for a twist. Every cell of the result still passes truck's acceptance test. A division that is still splitting after 64 sweeps (a jump) spends the face's evaluation budget, so it is refused by name exactly as before (#1536). It never comes back as a grid with a wall in it.
2. **Slivers: the parameter plane was 350x too short across.** truck triangulates a trimmed face by constrained Delaunay in (u, v). With nothing to constrain the plane next to the boundary, the empty-circle rule joined boundary points to the far ends of the strip. The new `step_stretch` stretches the faster parameter of a B-spline/NURBS face by its mean-speed ratio, so the mesher's plane has about the same proportions as the face. A face within 4:1 is untouched.
3. **The hole: boundary points found on the wrong turn.** truck's no-hint presearch (a 51 x 51 grid) samples a 14-turn strip about three times a turn, and Newton then settles one pitch off, outside the knot domain. On a root band the extrapolated rulings meet other turns exactly, at u = 7 on [0, 1]. The new `step_nearest` re-searches any answer that is off the surface or outside the domain. It starts Newton from the nearest samples of a grid that has up to 4 samples in every knot span (<= 4,096 evaluations), and takes the nearest answer inside the domain. Poles are settled by `step_pole` first (#1548), as before.

Decision entry: `docs/decisions/1602-thread-strip-mesh.md`.

## Readings (release; the user's files stay local)

| File | upstream main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 10208.STEP | 6,095,454 facets, chord 0.0157 mm (reduced), 31-72 s | **13,662 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.9 s** |
| 32050.STEP | 4,970,604 facets, 62-130 s | **8,128 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.8 s** |
| sc_logo.step | 36,728 facets, 0.19 s | 34,496 facets, 0.19 s, 0 open edges |
| synthetic 14-turn flank (a scratch generator) | 7,540,126 facets, 248 s, 3.3 GB | 3,072 facets, 0.8 s |
| the test's 4-turn trimmed flank | 471,695 facets, 7.3 s | 861 facets, 0.08 s |
| testdata/models/*.step | | facet counts unchanged |

**Closed-shell check:** I trial-merged PR #1576's head (e7d78efe) locally, without pushing it. Both parts import closed and pass its check. Before this change that check refused them: 10208 at face #1073 (up to 3.0 mm) and 32050 at faces #3350 and #5466. The gaps #1576's check still reported on these files are this issue's faces, and they are gone now.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs::a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count`: a STEP thread flank generated in the test (our own geometry, no user file), with run-out trims that cross the strip on the bias. It asserts fewer than 5,000 facets (471 K before), full chord, no triangle edge >= 2 mm, every facet within 0.01 mm of the ideal flank, and area within 1 % of the trimmed ideal.
- `step_division::tests`: `a_strip_curved_only_along_v_is_not_split_across_u`, `a_doubly_curved_patch_splits_both_ways`, `a_twist_the_chords_miss_still_splits_both_ways`, `a_jump_is_reported_as_not_converged`, `a_bad_tolerance_returns_the_corners`.
- `step_nearest::tests`: `a_point_on_a_many_turn_flank_is_found_on_its_own_turn`, `a_point_on_a_root_band_is_found_inside_the_knot_domain`, `a_point_off_the_face_keeps_trucks_answer`, `the_sample_grid_covers_every_span_within_its_bound`, `a_rescue_never_answers_outside_the_knot_domain`, `an_exact_answer_outside_the_domain_gives_way_to_one_on_the_surface_inside`, `a_nearer_answer_replaces_a_far_one_off_the_surface`.
- `step_stretch::tests`: `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters`, `the_faster_direction_is_stretched_by_the_ratio`.
- `step_guard::tests`: `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane`, `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn`. The existing `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` and `nothing_keeps_running_after_a_refused_pass` still hold.

## Mutation checks

Each guard was broken by hand, the named test was run, and then the guard was restored (`git status` clean after each run):

| # | Guard broken | Test that went red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | per-direction flags -> split both | `a_strip_curved_only_along_v_is_not_split_across_u` |
| M2 | twist fallback removed | `a_twist_the_chords_miss_still_splits_both_ways` |
| M3 | sweep cap returns the grid instead of `None` | `a_jump_is_reported_as_not_converged`, `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` |
| M4 | `meter.exhaust()` on no convergence removed | `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` |
| M5 | bad-tolerance guard removed | `a_bad_tolerance_returns_the_corners` (a hang, caught by its 20 s timeout) |
| M6 | stretch off (`Stretch::NONE`) | `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_...` (a 12 mm triangle), `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M7, M7b, M7c | u/v, second and mixed derivative scaling removed | `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M8 | parameter range left unscaled | `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M9 | rescue in `search_nearest_parameter` removed | `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn` |
| M10 | rescue in `search_parameter` removed | `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn` |
| M11 | out-of-domain answers no longer retried | `a_point_on_a_root_band_is_found_inside_the_knot_domain` |
| M12 | in-domain filter on candidates removed | `a_rescue_never_answers_outside_the_knot_domain` |
| M13 | "on the surface" clause removed | `an_exact_answer_outside_the_domain_gives_way_to_one_on_the_surface_inside` |
| M13b | "nearer" clause removed | `a_nearer_answer_replaces_a_far_one_off_the_surface` |
| M15 | stretch threshold 4 -> 1 | `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters` |
| M16 | stretch cap 1e6 removed | `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters` |

Not separately killable: replacing the selection guard with `if true` (always take the in-domain candidate). Taking it changes nothing unless Newton, started from in-domain samples, settles inside the domain farther from the point than truck's own answer. I found no fixture where that happens, because the runs go to the unconstrained nearest point and are then filtered out (M12). The guard stays as a defensive line.
An aspect-balancing pass that I tried during the work was dropped: its mutation left every test green, and the real files close without it.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: the app lib and 11 suites by gate map, among them `import_step_corner_blend` (#1548 pole), `import_step_guard`, `step_fidelity`, `step_budget` and `large_models`, plus the new `import_step_thread`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The `testdata/models/*.step` facet counts match upstream main, and `bspline_discontinuous.step` is still refused with the same message.

## Not exercised

- The heavy-lane `a_smooth_face_needing_more_than_the_old_cap_is_divided_not_tripped` (#1568, release `--ignored`) was not run.
- The UI import path was not run. The change is below `step::parse`, which every door shares.
- The real-file closure was checked only on a local trial merge with #1576, which is not on main.
- Windows and macOS were not run.

Changelog: STEP import meshes rational B-spline thread faces at full fidelity in seconds (about 10 K facets instead of 5-6 M per part, and no hole), splitting each parameter direction only where it is curved

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.19.0.

Fixes #1602
